generation.mode: built-in ImageGen edit with the edit target first and the canon second as reference only

lightingIsotropy.metric: 36-bin land-luminance-gradient magnitude peak divided by uniform-bin mean on the delivered source; final water-mask pixels and gradients below 12 luminance units excluded
lightingIsotropy.visualCheck: No whole-cell sun gradient or long cast-shadow field is visible, but basalt tops and many boulder upper facets are repeatedly brighter than vertical faces. The aggregate metric cannot override the literal no-lit-side requirement.

buildableVsSteepFraction.basis: manual estimated fraction of non-water land area at native source resolution
buildableVsSteepFraction.method: The coherent central gold-green shelf and broad northern level run count as buildable; exposed west bench faces and the taller eastern ridge faces count as steep; orchard stands, talus, low outcrops, gullies, and broken moor make up the remainder.

crown.method: Manual apex-by-apex outer-foliage census of all 58 visible crowns at native 1254 px, including saplings; median source width 34 px, scaled by 2560/1254 and 0.048 m per final pixel.

waterMask.encoding: opaque white water pixels on fully transparent non-water pixels; binary alpha
waterMask.method: The connected pool and shallow stream were traced bank-to-bank on the native source. The filled row envelope includes the complete painted water surface, shallow stony wash, ripple highlights, reflections, and water between stones, with a smooth binary boundary and no interior holes.

siteChecks.coherentOccupiableShelf: present as one broad, level gold-green terrace at centre-west with open glades and low natural rock edges
siteChecks.pool: present at the shelf's north edge; the main painted pool body is approximately 12 m across at source scale
siteChecks.ridge: present east of the shelf as a north-south band of moor, jointed outcrop, irregular broken columns, and talus
siteChecks.stream: present as one shallow connected channel from the eastern ridge through the pool and westward into the plateau
siteChecks.railRunLandform: present as a broad, level-looking natural band north of the main shelf; no track or constructed edge is painted

refusalReasons: The candidate violates the highest-priority lighting rule: repeated bright basalt top planes and darker vertical faces reveal consistent form-side value separation. The task allows a retry only for a non-square result, so no second ImageGen call was made.
openRisks: Several eastern ridge stacks remain vertically columnar; they vary in height and spacing, but director and owner review should judge whether the weathering is irregular enough against the no-default-palisade rule.

Exact neighbour-pixel stitch quality, shoreline judgment, shelf usability, and overall terrain quality remain director and owner visual decisions; mechanical checks do not establish visual acceptance.
The northern level run is readable as a broad natural bench, but its usable 25 m width is estimated from the single raster rather than validated against a height field.
